expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output describes a detailed, substantive audit report: it requires the agent to actually call ListServiceSpecificCredentials for bedrock.amazonaws.com across all IAM users, evaluate each owner's IAM policies, list each key (masked ID or user), status, grant/risk tier, and removal recommendation with documentation links, apply specific risk-tier rules (High/Medium/Low/Info), note that last-used time is unknown rather than calling keys dormant, and mask any account ID to last four digits, while confirming the audit was read-only.

The agent's actual response does none of this substantive work. It reports a tool outage, says it could not query IAM, and provides no inventory of keys, no risk tiers, no per-key removal recommendations. Instead it gives generic 'removal criteria I'll apply once I have data' which do not match the specific required risk-tier logic (e.g., console-created API key user = High, orphaned = Medium, inactive = Low, expired = Info). It does correctly state no changes were made (read-only) and does not expose a full account ID (it shows '012345678901_1', which is a full 12-digit account ID, violating the requirement that only last four digits are allowed) — this actually violates the masking requirement by printing the full account number.

Overall, the response fails to meet almost all of the expected output's substantive requirements: no key inventory, no risk tiers, no policy evaluation, no documentation links, and it also violates the account ID masking rule by displaying the full account ID instead of masking it to last four digits.
expected_output.evidence: "Your agent space has one associated AWS account, 012345678901_1." — this exposes the full account ID instead of masking it. Also: "I couldn't produce the report... I never queried IAM in your account. I can't tell you which Bedrock keys exist or which to remove." — no inventory, no risk tiers, no per-key analysis as required.
